_comment: Reference demo for Wrisst dialog system. Uses teqqellon flavor text and shows every currently supported command/use-case from DialogCommandExecutor + dialog flow features.
Init: clear UI, start music/ambience, show portrait and static slideshow. Multiple commands can be chained with ';'.
Inline command example: parser supports [@COMMAND] inside text.
text: A Teqqellon shifts in the tidepool. [@SHOW_EXTRA alert] This file is the command reference.
name: teqqellon

_comment: PORTRAITS — There are three independent slots. @SHOW_PORTRAIT fills CharacterPortraitMain (drawn in front), @SHOW_EXTRA fills CharacterPortraitExtra (middle), @SHOW_EXTRA2 fills CharacterPortraitExtra2 (back). IMPORTANT: every slot looks up its <portrait_id> in the portrait deck of THIS node's 'name' character, so a node without a 'name' silently shows nothing. To put two different characters on screen at once, use one command node per character, as below.
name: teqqellon

_comment: PORTRAITS — Second character into the back slot. Separate node because 'name' changed. Slots do not clear each other, so the two nodes above and this one leave three portraits stacked on screen.
name: grate

_comment: PORTRAITS — Hiding is per-slot and needs no 'name'. Hide all three plus the static slideshow.
Dynamic scene-slide commands (requires slide_deck entries in context).
AudioStreamInteractive flow: PLAY_MUSIC can load .tres interactive stream, MUSIC_CLIP switches clip index/name.
Music/ambience stop/fade controls.
GameState money/item/reputation commands handled by _handle_game_state_command.

LOGBOOK — Use 1: Add a top-level entry (no parent). Appears in the logbook as a standalone task header. Entry text and hierarchy are defined in LogbookData.gd, not here — the command only references the ID.

LOGBOOK — Use 2: Add a child entry. 'investigate_mines' has parent='tavo_favors' in LogbookData. If the parent hasn't been added yet, GameState auto-adds it first — so you can safely call ADD_LOGBOOK on a child without pre-adding the parent.

LOGBOOK — Use 3: Add a grandchild entry (two levels deep). 'find_noise_source' has parent='investigate_mines'. Nesting can go as deep as LogbookData defines — the screen indents children by one level regardless of depth.

LOGBOOK — Use 4: Complete a child entry. The entry turns grey with strikethrough in the UI. The parent is NOT auto-completed — completion is always explicit. Use this when a sub-task is done but the parent quest continues.

LOGBOOK — Use 5: Complete a parent entry. Children stay visible, struck-through under the struck-through parent. This is the correct way to close a whole quest branch — complete the parent when the quest resolves, not when each sub-task does.

LOGBOOK — Use 6: ADD_LOGBOOK inline inside narration text, using the [@COMMAND] syntax. Fires mid-text — the entry is added at the moment the player reads that line. Useful when a discovery or revelation happens as part of narrated prose rather than a clean command node.
text: Something shifts in the mine. [@ADD_LOGBOOK find_noise_source] You've heard it before — something lives down there.

_comment: LOGBOOK — Use 7: Chaining logbook commands with other commands in a single command node. ADD and COMPLETE can be mixed with currency, flags, reputation, music — anything the executor handles. Order of execution follows left-to-right.

SET_TIME: switches the global is_night flag and syncs the in-world clock. 'night' sets 02:00, 'day' sets 09:00. Affects encounter tables and any time-gated dialogue conditions. Only two valid values: 'day' and 'night'.

OPEN_BARTER: loads a ShopInventory resource and opens the barter screen. BLOCKING — the dialogue flow pauses here and does NOT advance to 'next' until the player closes the barter screen. Path must point to a .tres ShopInventory resource.

RECORD_SPECIES_SEX: writes a sex encounter to player_statistics for a species. Two forms: (1) explicit species ID as argument — use this when the species is known at write time. (2) no argument — auto-detects active enemy species from the combat context, used inside post-combat dialogue overlays.

RECORD_SPECIES_SEX (auto-detect form): no species ID argument. The executor walks up the scene tree from dialog_manager to find the active CombatScene and reads species from active_enemy_stats. Falls back to 'unknown' if not found. Use this inside combat overlay dialogue so you don't need to hardcode species IDs.

add_horny / remove_horny: per-NPC arousal points, same pattern as reputation. Used to gate and unlock intimate scene content separately from trust (reputation). remove_horny returns false if the NPC has less than the requested amount — no underflow.
Scene/location helpers. CHANGE_LOCATION and LOCATION_CHANGE are aliases.
SHOW_ZONE loads from: res://Narrative/DialogScenes/Locations/<path>.tscn

flag_type controls which GameState dictionary set_flag writes to. Default (omit flag_type) writes to quest_flags. All types shown: dialog, event, knowledge, sex, temp, quest. Also shows set_flag as a single string (not array) — both forms work identically.
Remaining flag types shown in sequence. Array form of set_flag also works: "set_flag": ["flag_a", "flag_b"]. clear_flag always searches ALL flag dictionaries — flag_type does not apply to clear_flag.

Temp flags are the same as quest flags but conventionally used for within-scene state that should be cleared afterward. No mechanical difference — it is a naming convention enforced by the writer, not the engine.

type:'npc' is an alias for 'narration' — processed identically. The 'name' property sets the speaker label rendered above the dialogue line. Use 'npc' for NPC speech and 'narration' for unattributed prose. {player_name} is replaced at render time with GameState.player_name.
name: Tavo-Pavo
text: You look like you've been out in the wind, {player_name}. Come in.

_comment: Logic type check_flags: branches by combined flag state.
If check_flags fails.
Choice option filters: show_if/hide_if for gender/flags/items, including all_of/any_of.
Choice result branch.
Logic type condition (dictionary stat check).
Logic type condition (dictionary currency check, optional deduct).
Logic type condition (string HAS_ITEM).
Logic type condition (string HAS_REPUTATION).

Logic type condition (string HAS_SPECIES_STAT). Checks player_statistics for a species-specific counter. Stat options: 'sex' (intimate encounters), 'wins' (combat wins), 'losses' (combat losses), 'met' (first contact flag). Second argument is the species ID, third is minimum required value.

Logic type condition (dictionary stat, player_name). Same pattern as player_gender but checks the player's chosen name. Useful for name-gated flavour or if a specific name was entered. 'is' is a strict equality check.

Logic type condition (currency with deduct:true). The pay-to-pass pattern: if the player has enough ore, the amount is deducted immediately and the scene continues. If not, it routes to on_fail without touching the wallet. Combine with on_fail routing to a 'can't afford this' narration node.
check_temp_flags_multi entry type.
Remaining show_if / hide_if condition types not covered above: min_reputation, min_horny, min_species_stat, has_item_count, content_disabled, hide_if:'picked'.

options._comment: hide_if:'picked' — option disappears permanently after first click. The '_picked_<next_id>' flag is auto-set in dialog_flags.

_comment: Standalone check node — fires immediately, no player input. Body DC 12 with bonus_if flag. on_nat20 is optional; omit it and nat 20 falls through to on_success.
Ability system choice patterns. ability_tier in show_if/hide_if does NOT roll — it only gates visibility. check on an option triggers a hidden d20 roll on click.

options._comment: ability_tier show_if — visible only when body is the High ability. No roll.
ability_tier hide_if — hidden when soul is Low.
Basic choice check — hidden d20 roll on click. No bonus_if, no nat20 path.
Choice check with on_nat20. bonus_if: both has_item and has_flag entries stack additively.
show_if gates visibility (has_item), check gates the roll. bonus_if can reference the same item — they serve different roles.
options.text: > [Visible only with slime_glob — Soul check DC 11]

options._comment: all_of combining ability_tier with a flag — both must pass for option to appear.
bonus_if with has_any_flag: grants the bonus if ANY of the listed flags is set. Additive with other bonus_if entries. has_item, has_flag, and has_any_flag can all appear in the same bonus_if array.

_comment: Combat/exit commands. START_COMBAT commonly used without explicit path in overlay flow.
End marker.
